meta.title: Amazon's Retail Business Barely Turns A Profit. This Division Pays For Everything.
meta.hook: Amazon's massive retail operation runs on razor-thin margins. Almost all its profit comes from somewhere else entirely.
meta.description: Amazon's North America and international retail segments generate huge revenue but thin operating margins, functioning more like a customer-acquisition engine than a profit center. The real profit driver is Amazon Web Services, its cloud computing division: a much smaller slice of total revenue that delivers an outsized share of total operating income. Retail scale funds AWS's infrastructure buildout, and AWS profit funds everything else.

scenes.narration: Amazon's massive retail operation runs on razor-thin margins. Almost all its profit comes from somewhere else.

visual.visual_intent: A vast fulfillment center with boxes moving on conveyor belts, industrial light, wide tracking shot
visual.decision_reason: hook beat: the retail machine, hard cut

scenes.narration: Selling and shipping products at scale is expensive. Warehouses, delivery trucks, packaging, all eating into a thin margin.

visual.decision_reason: shows the cost side of retail

scenes.narration: The real profit engine is a division most customers never think about: Amazon Web Services, its cloud computing arm.

scenes.narration: AWS makes up a much smaller slice of Amazon's total revenue, but it consistently delivers the majority of the company's operating profit.
